Gender.rationale: Ironclad.cs:24 `CharacterGender.Masculine`, read only by `AddDetailsTo` (CharacterModel.cs:246-255) to feed pronoun LocStrings. Purely grammatical/UI text; the `Character` dataclass (characters.py) has no gender concept and needs none.

UnlocksAfterRunAs.rationale: Ironclad.cs:29 returns `null` (starts unlocked, matching the C# doc comment). `UnlocksAfterRunAs` feeds `GetUnlockText`/`SaveManager.Instance.GenerateUnlockStateFromProgress` (CharacterModel.cs:260-276), a save-file meta-progression system the sim does not model at all — the sim trains within ONE run and has no cross-run unlock state. `events/orobas.py`'s own docstring already states the sim's deliberate stance explicitly ("the sim models a fully-unlocked run"), consulted from `base.Owner.UnlockState.Characters` at `Orobas.GenerateInitialOptions` (Orobas.cs:187-194) — that event record's deliberate-divergence is the consumption-side counterpart of this waiver; not re-derived here, cited for consistency.

NameColor.rationale: Ironclad.cs:31 `StsColors.red`, a Statistics-screen text color (CharacterModel.cs:48-51). No sim reader; presentation only.

StartingGold.rationale: Ironclad.cs:35 `StartingGold => 99`. Exact match. All five characters share this constant in the C# too (verified by reading all five Characters/*.cs files), so it is not Ironclad-specific.

CardPool.rationale: Ironclad.cs:37 `ModelDb.CardPool<IroncladCardPool>()`. RE-EXECUTED, not inherited from the prior card-tier finding: `IroncladCardPool.GenerateAllCards` (IroncladCardPool.cs:22-97) lists 87 cards; `sts2_rl.cards.pool.IRONCLAD_POOL` has 85. The 2-card gap is NOT a divergence: `Tank.cs:14` and `DemonicShield.cs:16` both declare `MultiplayerConstraint => CardMultiplayerConstraint.MultiplayerOnly` — the only two cards in the whole 87-card list that do — and the sim is single-player-only by design (the shared contract's own multiplayer-params exclusion), with no card class registered for either id (`'tank' in _CARD_CLASSES` and `'demonic_shield' in _CARD_CLASSES` both False, confirmed by import). 87 - 2 = 85, exact. The remaining 85 ids were spot-checked at both ends (first, last and several interior entries) and the total matches a prior independent count cited in `audit/records/relic/kaleidoscope.json` ("1 character pool of 85 cards"). Per-card fidelity of those 85 is the `card` kind's own subject (202 records) and is cited, not re-derived, here.

PotionPool.rationale: Ironclad.cs:39 `ModelDb.PotionPool<IroncladPotionPool>()`, whose `GenerateAllPotions` (IroncladPotionPool.cs:19-22) is literally `Ironclad4Epoch.Potions`. RE-EXECUTED: `sts2_rl.potion_pools.IRONCLAD_POTION_POOL` has exactly 3 entries (`blood_potion` common, `soldiers_stew` rare, `ashwater` uncommon) and the sim treats every epoch as unlocked (same fully-unlocked design as the card pool and relic pool, per `IroncladPotionPool.GetUnlockedPotions`'s epoch gate being irrelevant under that design). Per-potion fidelity is the `potion` kind's own subject (51 records, already audited) and is not re-derived here.

RelicPool.rationale: Ironclad.cs:41 `ModelDb.RelicPool<IroncladRelicPool>()`. RE-EXECUTED: `IroncladRelicPool.GenerateAllRelics` (IroncladRelicPool.cs:19-29) lists exactly 8 relics (Brimstone/BurningBlood/CharonsAshes/DemonTongue/PaperPhrog/RedSkull/RuinedHelmet/SelfFormingClay) and `sts2_rl.relic_pools.IRONCLAD_RELIC_POOL` has the same 8 ids with the same rarity tags. `SharedRelicPool.cs`'s 118-relic count also matches `SHARED_RELIC_POOL`'s length exactly (118), so the two pools that make up Ironclad's full visible relic set (8 + 118 = 126) are both accounted for at the membership-count level. Per-relic fidelity is the `relic` kind's own subject (260 records, already audited) and is not re-derived here. NOTE FOR THE NEXT BATCH: the campaign brief for this batch stated "1 relic missing from the Ironclad-visible pools" as an inherited finding from a prior round; this batch could not corroborate that figure by a membership-count check (both pool lists match their C# counterparts exactly) and did not have budget to chase it through the `relic` kind's 260 records individually. Not resolved here — flagged as an open citation for whoever owns it next.

StartingDeck.rationale: Ironclad.cs:43-55: 5x StrikeIronclad, 4x DefendIronclad, 1x Bash, in that literal array order. `characters.py`'s tuple is `('strike',)*5 + ('defend',)*4 + ('bash',)`, the exact same order. Order is parity-critical per the module's own docstring (deal order feeds the combat-start shuffle) and matches exactly, not just as a multiset.

StartingRelics.maps_to: Character(starting_relics=('burning_blood',)) (characters.py:109), granted at run.py's enter_first_act (the per-relic grant loop preceding the act roll)
StartingRelics.rationale: Ironclad.cs:57 `ModelDb.Relic<BurningBlood>()`. RE-VERIFIED, per this batch's brief, that the prior fix (granting Burning Blood at all) is STILL true today: `run.py`'s `enter_first_act` iterates `self.character.starting_relics` and calls `self.add_relic(relic_id)` for each, mirroring `Player.PopulateStartingRelics` (Player.cs:739-748), which the constructor calls unconditionally (Player.cs:341). `burning_blood` is a registered relic class (`'burning_blood' in ALL_RELICS` -> True, confirmed by import) and its own record (a prior round's subject, not re-derived here) is the +6-HP-per-combat heal this exact grant was found missing for. The sim's loop carries one extra guard C# does not have (`if not any(r.id == relic_id for r in self.relics)`), which is a harmless idempotency check under the game's actual call order (relics list is always empty at this point in a fresh run) rather than a divergence.

GetArchitectAttackVfx.rationale: Ironclad.cs:75-92, five VFX asset-path strings used only when this character attacks the TheArchitect victory event. Purely visual asset selection, no damage/gameplay math; the sim's Architect-event handling (if any) does not need a VFX list.

GenerateAnimator.rationale: Ironclad.cs:94-118, builds a Godot animation state graph (adds a `heavyAttack` branch over the CharacterModel base). Pure presentation.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: INHERITED from CharacterModel.cs:208 (`=> false`; Ironclad.cs itself declares no override). A CharacterModel never participates in the combat hook-listener system in the game; the sim's `Character` dataclass (characters.py) is a pure stat/pool table with no `hook_*` methods and is never registered as a listener anywhere — the same fact stated from the other side. Both engines agree characters are not hook participants, so there is nothing to diverge on despite the sim carrying no explicit flag for it.

guards.what: BaseOrbSlotCount / MaxEnergy — declared on CharacterModel itself (CharacterModel.cs:84/:88) as VIRTUAL, not abstract, and Ironclad.cs overrides neither, so neither appears as a declared OR inherited override for this unit under `split_overrides`'s one-level base-following (the defaults live on the immediate base, which is not itself walked a second level).
guards.maps_to: `Character.max_energy` defaults to 3 and `Character.base_orb_slot_count` defaults to 0 (characters.py:79/:81) and Ironclad's row overrides neither — matching the C# default exactly for both.

None of CharacterModel.cs's members route through `AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension` anywhere in the five Characters/*.cs files (verified by reading all five) — a character's stats are ascension-INVARIANT; ascension instead scales monster/relic/card values elsewhere. Out of this kind's scope per PROMPT.md's own "Ascension values: out of scope" line, and moot here regardless since there is nothing ascension-scaled to check.
